planting.note: Plant nursery transplants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Princeton was selected long before Dutch elm disease became widespread, purely for form and vigor, and only later proved to carry unusually strong disease tolerance, making it one of the most widely planted elm replacements today.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, allowing generous room for the tree's wide, arching, classic vase-shaped canopy to develop. Princeton is a selection of American elm originally chosen in the 1920s for its fast growth, dense glossy foliage, and handsome symmetrical form, only to later prove one of the most Dutch-elm-disease-tolerant American elm selections available, which has made it the standard replacement elm for streets, parks, and campuses across much of the country. It restores the soaring, cathedral-like street-tree silhouette that made American elm so beloved before the disease devastated the species, while resisting infection far better than seedling-grown trees. Water deeply during establishment, provide good air circulation and avoid wounding the bark, since even resistant cultivars can occasionally succumb under heavy disease pressure, and prune to maintain a strong central structure while the young tree is developing its canopy.
